slot.brief: Ask which pollutant(s) cause ozone depletion and which cause acid rain / photochemical smog (identify by chemical reaction).

stem:
Consider the following atmospheric chemical reactions:

(I) $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}(g) + \text{O}(g) \rightarrow \dot{\text{Cl}}(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$

(II) $\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{SO}_3(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$

(III) $\text{NO}_2(g) \xrightarrow{h\nu} \text{NO}(g) + \text{O}(g)$

These reactions are primarily associated with which environmental phenomena, respectively?
options: Ozone depletion, acid rain, and photochemical smog
Ozone depletion, photochemical smog, and acid rain
Acid rain, ozone depletion, and photochemical smog
Photochemical smog, acid rain, and ozone depletion

verdicts.working: Reaction I: ClO• + O → Cl• + O2 is the chlorine radical catalytic cycle destroying stratospheric ozone (ozone depletion). Reaction II: SO2 oxidized by O3 to SO3, which forms H2SO4 with moisture (acid rain). Reaction III: photolysis of NO2 gives NO + O, the initiating step of photochemical smog. Order matches option A.

working:
1. Reaction (I): $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}(g) + \text{O}(g) \rightarrow \dot{\text{Cl}}(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$ represents the regeneration of reactive chlorine free radicals ($\dot{\text{Cl}}$) from chlorine monoxide radicals in the stratosphere, maintaining the catalytic cycle of ozone depletion.

2. Reaction (II): $\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{SO}_3(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$ represents the ozone-promoted oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ in the troposphere. The resulting $\text{SO}_3$ combines with rain droplets to form $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, causing acid rain.

3. Reaction (III): $\text{NO}_2(g) \xrightarrow{h\nu} \text{NO}(g) + \text{O}(g)$ is the primary photochemical initiation step in the formation of photochemical smog, generating nascent oxygen atoms that subsequently react with $\text{O}_2$ to produce tropospheric ozone and peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN).

Hence, the correct sequence is ozone depletion, acid rain, and photochemical smog.

Independent check: Reaction I: ClO• + O → Cl• + O2 is the chlorine radical catalytic cycle destroying stratospheric ozone (ozone depletion). Reaction II: SO2 oxidized by O3 to SO3, which forms H2SO4 with moisture (acid rain). Reaction III: photolysis of NO2 gives NO + O, the initiating step of photochemical smog. Order matches option A.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option B: Confuses reaction (II) with photochemical smog because ozone is present, and mistakenly assigns the photolysis of $\text{NO}_2$ to acid rain.
Option C: Mistakenly assumes reaction (II) causes ozone depletion because $\text{O}_3$ is consumed, and confuses radical regeneration with acid rain.
Option D: Inverts reactions (I) and (III), confusing stratospheric radical chemistry with tropospheric photochemical smog initiation.
